name: Victorian manufacture
region: Britain, with its empire and the United States
summary: The household goods of the machine age in Britain: cast iron, pressed glass, deep-buttoned velvet and dark polished wood, with ornament added to each surface by the machine.

philosophy.core_thesis: The machine makes ornament cheap, so each object can carry rich pattern, deep colour and heavy form as a sign of comfort and rank.
design_principles: Cover each large surface with ornament: a turned, carved, moulded, pressed or printed pattern.
Use dark, deep polish on mahogany, walnut and oak; the gloss is 60 to 85 GU.
Use cast iron for stoves, baths, stands and fences, and cast the pattern in the mould.
Make a seat deep and soft, with buttoned velvet and a fringe of 5 to 10 cm.
Use pressed glass with a repeat pattern and coloured glass for lamps and vases.
Use 3 or 4 saturated colours in one room: crimson, bottle green, dark blue and gold.
Make each object with a heavy base and a rich top, so that it looks solid and costly.
anti_patterns: Visible fixings in a plain, steel style
A single clean line with no pattern

form.geometry: Curves and swells: the balloon, the cabriole, the bulb and the scroll, with a Gothic arch or a classical pediment on top.
form.silhouette: A heavy, closed outline with a wide base, rounded shoulders and a rich crest; a deep, rounded seat on short turned legs.
form.edges: Round and moulded edges with a radius of 5 to 20 mm and a bead or a step in the section.
form.proportion: A sideboard is about 120 cm high with a mirror back, 180 cm wide; a seat is deep, about 60 cm, and low, about 40 cm high.
form.ornament: Dense pattern in the mould, the turning, the print or the press: acanthus, ivy, Gothic tracery, a diaper or a fruit and flower garland.
rules: Each object carries at least 1 ornament band or pattern.
Each large wood surface has a turned, carved or moulded part.
A seat has buttoned upholstery and a fringe or a gimp edge.
Dark wood and deep colour cover more than 60% of the room's objects.
A glass or metal part has a pressed or cast repeat pattern.

materials.rule: Dark wood and cast metal make the body; velvet and glass carry the colour and the pattern; 0% of the visible surface is bare steel or plastic.

finish.gloss: 60–85 GU on polished wood, 80–95 GU on glaze and enamel, 10–30 GU on velvet
finish.patina: A deep, dark, even polish; the style accepts dust, soot and wear as signs of a well-used room, but not rust.

hardware.section: Rods and stems 15–30 mm; cast parts 4–10 mm thick
hardware.joints: Screws hidden under turned wood plugs or cast covers; mouldings and brass mounts hide each joint.
hardware.handles: A turned wooden knob, a porcelain knob with a printed pattern or a cast brass drop handle on a plate.
hardware.switches_and_taps: Before 1880 there is no electric switch; the period-faithful reissue is a turned brass rotary switch with a fluted knob. A tap is a pillar tap with a cross head in brass, over a fireclay sink.

palette.strategy: Deep, saturated colour on dark wood: crimson, bottle green and dark blue, lit with the gold of gilt and brass.

manufacture.scale: Factories with 100s to 1000s of workers; catalogues sold the same pattern to a whole country.
manufacture.signs: Repeat patterns of the same mould, the seam of a pressed glass and a fine, even machine turning.

objects.form: cast-iron roll-top bath on claw feet
turned rotary with a fluted knob (a period-faithful reissue)
gas bracket with a pressed shade
tall Gothic-revival case with a carved back
balloon-back chair with a carved rail
deep glazed Belfast sink on a brick pier
pressed coloured-glass vase with a moulded pattern

positive: studio product photograph, warm lamp light

emotion.target_response: Warm, heavy comfort and a sense of rank: the viewer sees a full, rich and well-fed room.

use_cases: period fittings for a Victorian terrace
a dark, rich library or parlour
a reissue of a roll-top bath or a pillar tap
a still life of pressed glass and brass
avoid_when: The brief asks for light, plain or minimal objects.
The room is small and needs low visual mass.

modifiers.how: Replace the machine ornament with plain oak, a visible joint and hammered copper.
Slim the legs, use pale grounds, fluting and gilt mounts in place of dense pattern.
Remove the ornament and the velvet; use maple, cherry and a thin oil.

era_blend.note: A contemporary reinterpretation keeps the style when it keeps the forms and the materials.
